anomalies.observed: The 'ATO Valve' block drives the ATO solenoid with T5, an AO3400A (small SOT-23 N-MOSFET), whose gate is pulled up to +3V3 by R12 (10 kΩ) and pulled down by T4 (BT3904) driven through R10 (100 Ω).
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table states the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is T3, an AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET), gate driven through R10 (100 Ω) and pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).
ATO Valve block: ATO_VALVE → R10 100Ω → T4 BT3904; T5 AO3400A with R12 10k to +3V3, C11 47µ, D4 SS34, P4 MC_0.2"

anomalies.impact: The AO3400A is a much smaller device than the specified AON6407 (higher Rds(on), far lower thermal/current capability). Switching the 24 V ATO solenoid with it may cause overheating or failure of the valve driver, defeating the automatic top-off function.

parsed.summary: The design largely matches the specification (I2C pull-ups 2.2 kΩ, TMC2209 sense resistors 110 mΩ, pump/valve gate resistors 100 Ω, buck feedback giving 5 V, isolated pH/EC channels, TMC2209 addresses 0/1/2), but the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is built with T5 (AO3400A) instead of the specified T3 (AON6407), a component substitution that would make the valve driver behave differently from the intended design.
